R1.reason: Both are the same effect: a cyan-blue additive glow or spark ball with a white-hot core and soft blue lobes around it, flickering from frame to frame.

R2.reason: Frames are the original's 32x32, but the effect fills them differently. The original is a broad, lumpy cloud of many overlapping soft blobs that reaches most of the frame in every frame (e.g. frames 5, 7, 8 and 10 spread nearly edge to edge). The reproduction is a compact, near-round white disc with a fairly hard edge and only one to three small lobes stuck to it (frames 0, 4 and 7 are almost plain discs). It leaves more of the frame empty (dark fraction 0.58 against 0.46) and loses the original's ragged, clustered outline.

R3.reason: Same cyan rim and white core as the engine blends them. The measured mean colour difference is 8.7, under 15. The reproduction's white core is a little larger and more saturated, but it is the same colour.

R4.reason: 11 frames, the same as the original. Both keep a steady brightness while the lobes shift around the core, which reads as the same flicker. Both envelopes are close to flat: first and last frames are 0.94 and 1 in the original, 0.89 and 0.89 in the reproduction. The loop closes without a dark end, as the original's does. The different peak position (1 against 0.2) is noise on a flat envelope. The reproduction's lobes jump about a bit more (jitter 1.77 against 1.51), but it is the same kind of motion.

R5.reason: The type (parallel) and format (additive) match the original's, and the frames read back at the same 32x32 size and count.
